chunks: What is I2C bus capacitance. The question: What is bus capacitance?
Bus capacitance is the total capacitance between an I2C wire and ground. Every chip pin, centimeter of trace, connector and length of cable adds a little.
Capacitance is a wire's reluctance to change voltage, since charge must be moved on or off it.
The pull-up must supply that charge each time the wire rises, so more capacitance means a slower rising edge.
The I2C spec caps it at 400 picofarads (picofarads) per line for Standard and Fast mode.
Think of heating a room with a small heater. The more furniture and wall to warm, the longer it takes.
The heater is the pull-up resistor, and the stuff to warm is the capacitance. Cooling is different. Opening a big window cools the room almost at once.
That is a chip pulling the wire low: falling edges are fast, rising edges slow.
Rise time is linear in C b for a given R p . 4. 7 kilohms meets Fast mode only up to 75 picofarads; 2. 2 kilohms up to 161 picofarads; 1 kilohms up to 354 picofarads.
Every line meets Standard mode at 100 picofarads.
Capacitance: how much charge a wire must take on to change its voltage ("What capacitance is"). Bus capacitance ( C b ): the total capacitance from one bus wire to ground.
Each of SDA and SCL has its own. Pin capacitance: the small capacitance each chip pin adds, typically 2 to 10 picofarads.
Pull-up resistor: the resistor that charges the wire back to high. Rise time: how long the wire takes to go from 30% to 70% of the supply.
A bus has an MCU pad (7 picofarads), 5 sensors at 6 picofarads each, a connector (3 picofarads), 12 cm of trace at 1. 2 picofarads per centimeter, and a couple of test points.
That is about 56 picofarads. With a 4. 7 kilohms pull-up, the rise time is 0. 85 times 4700 times 56 picofarads about 223 nanoseconds. Now add a 1 m cable at about 100 picofarads.
The total is 156 picofarads, and the rise time is about 621 nanoseconds, which fails the 300 nanoseconds limit for 400 kilohertz. That is the whole idea.
"Bus capacitance is the total capacitance from an I2C line to ground: device pins and ESD structures, PCB trace, connectors and cable.
The pull-up has to charge it, so rise time is about 0. 85 times R p times C b . The spec caps it at 400 picofarads for Standard and Fast mode.
As a rule of thumb I use 5 to 10 picofarads per device and about 1 picofarads per centimetre of trace, and I measure the real rise time to confirm."
